speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) secondary to prematurity.

Based on your history of 33-week gestation and the immediate onset of symptoms like grunting, significant retractions, and cyanosis, the clinical picture strongly supports a diagnosis of Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The blood gas results showing respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia are classic for this condition in premature infants. While the chest X-ray is requested to confirm the diagnosis, the combination of prematurity, early onset, and these specific physical signs makes RDS the primary diagnosis.
